larry-david.blurb: The numbered grievance list genuinely bends the recap form instead of narrating six games in order, and it lands the petty-outrage register perfectly — Bruce losing by 28 and getting promoted is "like getting fired and then being handed a parking space," and the 4-4-4 split "somehow annoys me more t

yogi-berra.blurb: The aphorism engine actually generates new Yogi rather than quoting old Yogi — "Depth don't matter when the other fella's got altitude," "He's climbing in the rankings and drowning in the standings" — though a few stretches lean on the real quotes to do the work.

hunter-s-thompson.blurb: The MILE-marker structure gives it forward motion and "2028 is currently in a hospital gown asking for a lawyer" is excellent, but it leans on borrowed Thompson (the bat-country opener, "too weird to live") more than it invents its own.

fred-rogers.blurb: The gentlest possible register applied to a brutal week is a genuine bend — "anything mentionable is manageable" aimed at a 2.83-point loss, McFeely delivering the injury report — and the Bruce/Sean 209 observation ("two different stories") is the sharpest read of the week, though the sincerity thic

mike-tyson.blurb: Some real punch in the one-liners — "That's not a lead, that's a restraining order" and "You can't win a fight with pillows" — but the boxing frame flattens into the same beat every section (he fought, he lost, keep your hands up) instead of building.

samuel-l-jackson.blurb: "Say '2.67' Again" as a section head is the one genuinely clever structural move, but the all-caps intensity is one note for 2,000 words and the Ezekiel frame is bolted to the top and bottom rather than running through.

ron-burgundy.blurb: This is the standard six-games-in-order recap with catchphrases dropped in on a timer ("Great Odin's raven," "glass case of emotion," "I love lamp," "that escalated quickly"); the closing stay-classy roll call that names all twelve owners is the only part doing real work.
